title: <Dynamic component={...}>: Element Switching Without Full Re-Creation

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Imagine a picture frame on the wall where you can swap the photo inside. Instead of tearing down the entire wall and rebuilding it every time you want a new photo, the `<Dynamic>` tag keeps the frame mounted and cleanly swaps the component or tag inside.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `<Dynamic component={componentAccessor()}>` renders a component or HTML tag dynamically based on a reactive signal or prop. `import { Dynamic } from 'solid-js/web';`. You can pass either component functions (`<Dynamic component={MyComponent} />`) or HTML tag string names (`<Dynamic component="h1" />`). When the `component` signal updates, Solid swaps only the dynamic element.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `<Dynamic>` is a built-in control flow component implemented as a memoized factory. Because Solid components do not re-render, rendering dynamic elements conditionally via ternary expressions (`{type() === 'a' ? <A /> : <B />}`) creates and destroys reactive scopes repeatedly. `<Dynamic>` optimizes this by creating a single memoized root that evaluates `createComponent()` or `createElement()` only when the component constructor reference changes, passing reactive props through transparently.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Under the hood, `<Dynamic>` is defined as `createComponent(createMemo(() => { const c = props.component; if (typeof c === 'string') return createElement(c, props); return createComponent(c, props); }))`. It wraps the tag selection in a `createMemo`. When `props.component` changes from `'button'` to `'a'`, the memo re-evaluates, disposes the previous child Owner scope, and instantiates the new tag.

codeComparison.title: Nested Ternary Component Switching vs <Dynamic>
codeComparison.summary: Ternary trees for dynamic tags become unreadable; `<Dynamic>` cleanly maps runtime tags and components.

interviewGotchas.question: Can `<Dynamic>` accept both string HTML tag names and custom SolidJS component functions?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Tests knowledge of polymorphic component capabilities.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes. If `component` is passed a string (e.g. `'div'`, `'button'`, `'svg'`), `<Dynamic>` creates a native DOM element with the provided props. If `component` is passed a component function reference (e.g. `MyCustomButton`), it invokes `createComponent(component, props)`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Passing an invalid value like `null` or `undefined` to `component` will result in `<Dynamic>` rendering nothing (an empty text node).

interviewGotchas.question: How are props passed to `<Dynamic>` evaluated when the component changes?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of prop forwarding in Solid control flow.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Props passed to `<Dynamic component={tag()} {...otherProps} />` are wrapped in a reactive proxy. When `tag()` changes, the previous component instance and its reactive scope are disposed, and the new component is instantiated with the same reactive `otherProps` proxy without requiring re-binding.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not destructure props before passing them into `<Dynamic>`, as destructuring breaks prop reactivity.
